items.summary: This work considers multi-agent coordination with arbitrary information networks among the agents using a game-theoretic approach. A system designer aims to assign local utility functions to the agents to guide their actions toward a desired system objective. The performance of the assigned local utilities is measured by the well known pure price of anarchy (pPoA) metric that equals the ratio of the system objective at the worst pure Nash equilibrium of the corresponding game to the optimal system objective. Our aim is to derive the utility functions which optimize the pPoA-based performance guarantees for any given information network and system objective. We develop a linear program that derives the optimal pPoA for any arbitrary information network and arbitrary system objective. Our work is the first to solve optimal utility design for arbitrary networks; our techniques generalize previous approaches which considered only the full-information setting. For supermodular objective functions, we prove that counterintuitively, a fully communication-denied utility design is optimal irrespective of the original information network. For submodular system objectives, an exhaustive numerical analysis suggests that the optimal utility design is robust to communication failures even for this case. When the system objective is weighted maximum coverage, the marginal contribution utility design provably optimizes the pPoA for a wide variety of information networks of interest.

items.summary: The Earth That Heard   The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua's altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel's unfinished offering, Cain's failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. This version adds a new chapter on Cain, the altar, and the city of refuge — linking "from My altar you shall take him" (Exodus 21:14) to the Mishnah's ruling that one sentenced without a High Priest never goes free (Makkot 2:7), and to the discovery that Shechem itself is designated a city of refuge in Joshua 20:7. Additional sections trace Jacob's route from Sukkot to Shechem as a draft of Joshua's entry axis, the letter-midrash of "sotho" (Genesis 49:11) as a covering that was never performed, and the mechanical letter-echo of Shaddai hidden in Laban's Aramaic "Yegar Sahadutha" (Genesis 31:47).12:56 PM   The work explicitly separates three epistemic levels: Text — what the biblical text states; Reading — what emerges when distant passages are compared; and Implication — the larger interpretation suggested by the resulting structure. The pattern is tested quantitatively. The present essay contains 136 key verses. Using the Control Alphabet / Mandatory Root morphology developed in The Road and the Place, 100,000 permutations yield T1 = 11.23 and T2 = 24.12, with zero exceedances (p_MC ≈ 10⁻⁵; Phipson & Smyth, 2010). A Leave-One-Book-Out test shows no single Torah book is necessary for the signal (worst case: Genesis removed → Z = 10.61). A Leave-One-Motif-Out test shows no single root is necessary (worst: rbtz removed → Z = 16.01). A book-stratified null (Z = 19.93) confirms the effect is not an artifact of verse distribution. A top-10 ablation (Z = 3.95, p = 0.0013) shows the signal weakens but survives removal of the dominant motifs. A Foundation 12-Letter Split, stripping all 10 control letters rather than 7, yields Z = 4.17 — confirming the framework is not ad-hoc. Six benchmark anthologies were tested: the Ebal/Shechem axis is anomalous in all three validated methods; Covenant remains a positive control but significantly lower; Joseph, Tabernacle, and "the place that He will choose" are negative in all. An independent replication pilot tested whether the signal depends on the author's specific verse choices. Eight semantic criteria were defined — no roots, no letter analysis, no knowledge of any test results — and two independent language models selected Torah verses blind. Model A (243 verses) yielded T2 = 8.70; Model B (252 verses) yielded T2 = 9.84; the consensus of both (142 verses) yielded T2 = 8.51. All with zero exceedances. Only 22% of the essay's verses were also selected. The signal survives independent selection. A pre-registered protocol for three independent human readers is included (protocol hash: a577cb03...). The result does not statistically prove the theological interpretation; it shows that the textual concentration being interpreted is itself measurable and unusual under multiple independent approaches. A dual adversarial computational audit (LLM-assisted) verified the code, reproduced the numbers, identified and corrected all bugs, and rated the statistical appendix at 7.0

items.summary: Traditional large language models (LLMs) are scoped to individual user sessions, limiting their knowledge to a single conversation and preventing them from learning user preferences that evolve over time. Existing agentic memory systems address this limitation but generally operate at the individual-user level, restricting the public knowledge that could be shared across users to improve downstream responses. We introduce AIM (Agentic Interoperable Memory), a unified, privacy-aware memory framework that enables multi-agent, multi-user LLM systems to persistently manage private and shared memory. AIM dynamically classifies information as private, scoped to one user and inaccessible to others, or public, accessible to all users. It enforces index-level access controls so that private memories are retrievable only by their owner, protecting sensitive data while allowing beneficial shared knowledge to improve coordination and consistency. We also introduce MUMBench (Multi-User Memory Benchmark), a dataset of multi-user interactions containing private and shareable information across four domains. To our knowledge, MUMBench is the first public dataset designed to evaluate multiple memory operations, including retrieval, creation, update, and deletion, in a multi-user environment. Across three independent runs on MUMBench, AIM achieves 96.0% visibility classification accuracy, 58.8% strict operation accuracy, and 70.5% state-aware operation accuracy.

items.summary: Recent advances in AI-assisted mathematical discovery, program search, and formal reasoning motivate a practical design question: how can a long-horizon open problem be reorganized into a broad, falsifiable, and evidence-accountable human–AI search? We present a prospective candidate-engineering framework, grounded in a source-bound retrospective Phase-I design case on arithmetic dynamical structures relevant to the Hilbert–Pólya programme. The paper does not claim a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a completed Hilbert–Pólya realization, or a spectral identification of Riemann zeros. The framework has three layers. In Layer 1, a mathematician fixes a mathematical origin, permitted data, and an admissible transformation class; the present case uses a prime-symbolic origin, whereas a new mathematician-supplied basic idea begins a new Layer-1 record. In Layer 2, mathematician and AI jointly draft and version-freeze an AGENTS.md contract specifying candidate identity, lineage, gates, controls, portfolio policy, and stopping rules. In Layer 3, bounded AI work returns a source-linked evidence handoff for mathematician review. The accompanying roadmap requires a single candidate to establish an endogenous arithmetic source, orbit/repetition ownership, and a same-object zeta or determinant before stronger analytic and operator obligations are considered. The case comprises one early exploration entry and five system-family sessions. Its P1 Wiki retains catalogued provenance records rather than a common score of completed papers, theorems, or Route advances. No source-bound top-level direction documents an integrated same-object A0+A1+A2 chain in one natural candidate. We therefore motivate a broader but lineage-filtered candidate portfolio, screened early for arithmetic, clock, and determinant ownership rather than assembled retrospectively from partial successes. The associated Wiki is a provenance and navigation resource designed to preserve positive local results, controls, scoped failures, and reuse boundaries for subsequent researchers.

items.summary: This white paper examines the operational, financial, customer, governance, and leadership consequences arising when customer-facing artificial intelligence makes a commitment the enterprise did not intend to make. The central argument is that a machine-generated promise becomes an enterprise risk when a customer reasonably relies on the output or when organisational systems allow the machine to act on it. The resulting exposure extends beyond hallucination into authority, workflow, customer reliance, execution, redress, and accountability. The paper identifies four escalating customer-AI risk states: Answer, Recommendation, Decision, and Commitment. Exposure increases when generated language moves from information into enterprise obligation. To govern this transition, the paper introduces the Machine Promise Control Architecture, structured around Authoritative Truth, Intent Classification, Authority Envelope, Verification Gate, Escalation and Redress, and Promise Telemetry. Three case studies demonstrate how machine output acquires authority in different operating environments. Cursor shows how generated language became perceived company policy. Rite Aid illustrates machine classification entering customer-facing operational action without adequate safeguards. McDonald’s and IBM demonstrate how conversational interpretation errors propagate into transaction errors, fulfilment problems, rework, and customer impact. Across all three cases, the common failure occurs when machine output acquires credibility, workflow access, decision rights, or customer reliance without corresponding control. The paper further separates AI authority into three distinct permissions: Say, Decide, and Execute. It introduces Promise Surface Area as an executive management model for assessing exposure based on interaction volume, promise-capable intents, authority scope, and consequence. It also applies Six Sigma disciplines through Critical-to-Quality measures, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis, and the Cost of Poor Promise Quality, linking customer-AI governance directly to operating economics. The central proposition is that customer-facing AI should be governed as a complete decision system rather than as a conversational interface. Enterprises need explicit controls over what AI says, decides, and executes, alongside governed knowledge, deterministic verification, meaningful human escalation, decision lineage, promise-quality measurement, and structured incident recovery. The objective is controlled autonomy, with machine authority expanding only as quickly as the organisation’s ability to govern the resulting commitments.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 18 August 2026.

items.summary: Periodic multilayer mirrors for X-rays require a layer period held to about 0.02 nm, set by deposition rates held in the laboratory's own notebook. A large language model agent was given a target multilayer specification and read access to a laboratory archive. Deposition recipes were authored in the native recipe language of a magnetron sputtering system and submitted through a Model Context Protocol bridge of 17 tools in three tiers, with enforcement held in the control application. The target was a 30-bilayer Ru/C multilayer with a period of 6.85 nm, a pair chosen because each period is fitted as two layers. The agent could write only inside a working project of its own, so it could alter neither the calibration it read nor the measurements that scored it. Mirrors were scored against a human-authored reference by X-ray reflectivity, and the 3% acceptance threshold on relative period difference was fixed before deposition. Across four scored agent-authored depositions the relative period difference fell from 20% on the calibration as given to 2.26% after one measured-feedback iteration and 0.79% after a second. Sixteen failure modes of the agent-facing interface were identified. The result is bounded to the period, pair and chamber observed.
items.title: Agent-authored deposition recipes for X-ray multilayer mirrors: schema-bound LLM control of a magnetron sputtering system with reflectivity-verified outcomes

items.summary: Abstract What can a bounded system justify from its evidence, computation and memory, and what follows when those resources cannot settle its question? This paper develops a mathematical account of verification boundaries under explicit task, evidence and resource contracts. An evidence-based verifier cannot correctly decide a claim that takes different truth values within one evidence fiber. Generating hypotheses or recursively processing the same evidence does not remove that obstruction without an additional informative channel or premise. Related results separate semantic determination, effective computation and bounded implementation; show why some finite resource classes have incomparable attainable capabilities rather than one greatest evaluator; and characterize conditional limits on self-verification. Positive results complement these obstructions. Finite query-tree constructions characterize adaptive acquisition and relational answer selection under declared costs. Explicit finite-machine models provide attainable implementation families with accounted resources and transport bounds. For finite permitted procedure classes, maximal antichains characterize terminal guarantee feasibility; their limitations under continuation distinguish terminal comparison from compositional preservation. Probability is treated through separate objects: posterior belief, environmental stochastic assumptions and private algorithmic randomization. Failure of a deterministic guarantee supplies no premise-free probability estimate. The results support a typed verification protocol: accepted certificates justify scoped assertions, bounded dispatch returns unresolved outcomes when necessary, and multiple obstruction causes remain visible beneath any summary label. Soundness, termination, diagnostic completeness and implementation correspondence are separate obligations. The paper establishes conditional boundaries and attainable constructions for its specified classes, while leaving general model correspondence and unrestricted justified self-improvement as distinct questions. This public edition updates the previously deposited v6.3 release. It corrects editorial status and import-scope wording, clarifies that probabilistic continuation requires additional declared premises, and incorporates the reference correction. Mathematical statements and proofs are preserved. Earlier versions remain part of the publication history.

items.summary: Assistance can make a person's decision possible while leaving the person vulnerable to interpretive substitution and control of the available options. This paper develops a framework for adult disability support when will and preferences admit several warranted interpretations. Decision authorship is distinguished from causal responsiveness, functional performance, legal capacity, the validity of a particular act, and responsibility. A set-valued model separates semantic fidelity from authority over support and menus. Conditional results characterize compatible outcomes under interpretive uncertainty, changes under additional evidence, and the limited relation between menu expansion and compatibility. Counterexamples show that reversing every expressed preference satisfies sensitivity, that a constant outcome can satisfy fidelity, and that accurate selection within a restricted menu can coexist with an objectionable exclusion of alternatives. A temporal extension distinguishes learning about an earlier preference from forming a present preference through support. A finite branchwise result identifies when clarification permits compatible implementation despite an empty initial intersection. The normative discussion confronts CRPD Article 12, the Committee's corrected General Comment No. 1, selected provisions of the Mental Capacity Act 2005, and a prior proposal for interpretive support. A fictional community-participation decision demonstrates the audit, including disagreement, refusal, revision and supporter conflict. The resulting framework makes uncertainty and authority answerable without converting mathematical compatibility into permission to decide for another person. Empirical validation and case-specific legal application remain open.
items.title: Preserving Decision Authorship under Uncertain Interpretation of Will and Preferences in Adult Disability Support

items.summary: Lux AI Season 3 requires agents to act under partial observability, randomized episode level dynamics, and a best of five match structure that rewards both tactical execution and fast adaptation. We present HORIZON, a hierarchical agent that combines symmetry aware spatial perception, dual memory belief tracking, relic centric graph attention, information gain driven exploration, and an opponent conditioned policy mixture. HORIZON separates short horizon control from cross match meta reasoning, while auxiliary belief and world model objectives stabilize learning. Trained with PPO in a large scale JAX simulator, the resulting agent explicitly infers hidden game parameters and opponent style. Experiments show consistent gains in match win rate, episode win rate, adaptation gain, and league rating over strong recurrent and feed forward baselines.
items.title: Hierarchical Belief Modeling for Zero-Shot Opponent Adaptation in Partially Observable Multi-Agent Navigation

items.summary: Pre-registered results for Phase 22.D. The range-non-overlap criterion was to be tested on a genuinely unseen hold-out: Linear B sub-corpora from Thebes, Mycenae and Tiryns, harvested from DAMOS only after the pre-registration was published. The harvest yielded 617 tablets and 766 word tokens under the same L2_strict filter used for Knossos and Pylos, but fragmented across 27 series, of which only 3 reached the pre-declared minimum of 40 types. The pre-declared power gate required 5. No word-length class reached the 20-type floor, so the stratified primary test never ran. Verdict: TEST-VOID. With 3 observations the 99% prediction interval lower bound is -43.1 percent, an impossible value for a rate, which is precisely what the power gate exists to catch. The suspension of the Linear A / Linear B morphological gap imposed by Phase 22.B therefore becomes indefinite: the gap is real and is not a word-length artefact, but whether it demonstrates non-Mycenaean-Greekness remains untested. Descriptive figures are reported without verdict force. The only remaining route is the full DAMOS Knossos corpus rather than the def_strict subset. TERMINOLOGY: this project does not claim that Linear A "is not Greek"; the tested and rejected hypothesis is Mycenaean Greek. Pre-registration: doi 10.5281/zenodo.22749112. Version v2 (2026-09-15): OpenTimestamps proofs upgraded to confirmed Bitcoin block attestations. The pre-registration is anchored in blocks 966966, 966969 and 966971; the hold-out corpus and runner in blocks 967020, 967026 and 967042 — 54 blocks (approximately nine hours) later. The blindness of the test is therefore established by the Bitcoin blockchain rather than by declaration. No change to the data, the analysis, or the TEST-VOID verdict.
items.title: Phase 22.D Results: The Range Criterion Is Untestable on Available Unseen Mycenaean Data — A Pre-registered TEST-VOID Outcome.

A 139-case offline routing report contains 112 passes and 27 failures despite zero gating failures, because known gaps are explicitly exempted from the gate. Of the durations, 121 equal the signed 32-bit maximum and carry abandoned-client labels; inspected database code clamps elapsed lifecycle age. The pooled recorded 99th percentile is 2,147,483,647 ms, versus 38,118.31 ms among server-observed completed calls. This is a stratum contrast, not a treatment effect. In a documented single-trajectory compaction pilot, the reported follow-up input reduction is 94.39%, but the reduction across the trigger and follow-up calls together is 46.54%. items.summary: Languishing has predominantly been conceptualised at the level of the person, yet psychological constraint may also be expressed within particular configurations of thought. This qualitatively led mixed-methods study examined how university students’ person-level flourishing and NARMA languishing profiles related to self-identified cognitions that constrained movement towards personally meaningful flourishing futures. Seventy-five consenting participants at a South African university completed a 10-item NARMA Continuum comprising five PERMA-aligned flourishing indicators and five directly assessed NARMA languishing indicators: Negativity, Apathy, Restricted Relationships, Meaninglessness, and Adversity Preoccupation. Participants subsequently described a future flourishing self and completed a structured Target, Understand, Replace, and Nurture reflection. One consenting response contained insufficient substantive qualitative material, yielding 74 cases for qualitative analysis. Reflexive thematic analysis was combined with structured framework coding of three proposed properties of languishing cognition: Yield, the represented change in viable human possibility associated with a thought; Viability, the extent to which remaining possibility could still support meaningful participation; and Trajectory, the orientation of possibility towards narrowing, stalling, redirection, or widening. Quantitative scores were integrated as person-level case attributes. Target cognitions principally concerned anticipated failure or non-attainment (29.7%), stalled effort or mobilisation (20.3%), adversity or uncertainty (20.3%), and inadequacy or insufficient capability (13.5%). Yield was predominantly depletive (95.9%), yet depletion did not determine subsequent Trajectory. Viability was most commonly compromised but retained (56.8%), rather than extinguished, while Trajectory was mixed or redirecting in 48.6% of cases, narrowing in 21.6%, stalled in 16.2%, and widening in 13.5%. Overall flourishing and NARMA languishing were strongly inversely associated, r = -.762, 95% CI [-.843, -.647], p < .001. Exploratory integration showed that person-level flourishing differed across cognition-level Trajectory groups, H(3) = 12.69, p = .005, ε² = .14, whereas overall NARMA languishing did not, H(3) = 5.61, p = .132. Replacement cognitions most often restored agency through incremental progress, behavioural pathways, realistic self-permission, or action despite adversity. The findings support a cross-level distinction between person-level languishing and cognition-level constraint. They further suggest that the psychological significance of a thought may depend not only on its valence or content, but on what viable possibility it changes, what remains usable, and where possibility is oriented next. Keywords: languishing, NARMA, flourishing, cognition, viable human possibility, future selves, Yield, Viability, Trajectory, TURN
items.title: What Does a Languishing Thought Take, Leave, and Make Possible? A Qualitative Study of Yield, Viability, and Trajectory in University Student Cognition

items.summary: Abstract When does a transformed presentation remain the same for a declared task, what evidence can establish that judgment, and what can a bounded observer safely do with it? This paper separates representation, evidence, control and implementation, giving each an exact mathematical contract. For declared transformations and required observations, contextual indistinguishability determines the greatest observation-preserving congruence. Its quotient is the coarsest lawful representation preserving every demanded observation under every permitted continuation. A reference–current construction applies this result directly to persistence judgments, including breaking outcomes and required provenance. An evidence channel determines the demanded distinctions extensionally exactly when its kernel refines the contextual congruence; failure supplies an indistinguishable pair requiring different answers. For explicitly presented finite systems, the paper provides quotient constructions, separating witnesses, supplementary-information bounds and exact finite-memory criteria. Under declared transition and observation semantics, robust safety is characterized by a greatest fixed point, with checkable winning and losing certificates. Suitable observer quotients preserve the safety computation. Finite controller enumeration and declared sensor catalogues yield exact bounded-memory synthesis and joint resource frontiers; adaptive acquisition is incorporated as action under explicit contracts. The paper also establishes incremental and transport laws, strategic comparison results, and conservative model-to-system safety transfer under stated coverage hypotheses. Representation minimality, safety maximality and bounded implementation attainment remain distinct. Extensional existence does not imply effective discovery or affordability, and mathematical guarantees do not establish physical correspondence. The results characterize what can be preserved, distinguished and safely controlled within declared regimes while exposing the additional assumptions required for implementation and deployment. This public edition updates the previously deposited v19.1 release. It clarifies editorial framing, historical review status and correction lineage while preserving the mathematical content. Earlier versions remain part of the publication history.

items.summary: Structured quantum circuits are often represented by low-dimensional records such as occupation numbers or constraint feasibility rather than by full outcome distributions. A record loses control-dependent information when it merges outcomes whose probabilities respond differently to circuit parameters. We assess this loss without assuming a parametric hardware-noise model. Quantum Fisher information bounds premeasurement sensitivity; Fisher metrics of measurements and recorded statistics describe device-attainable sensitivity. For finite control changes, a Hellinger residual measures the response removed by a record, while its local quadratic term is the conditional covariance of the full-outcome score. Simultaneous confidence bounds support approval, refusal, or deferral. We prove a finite-library completion theorem: executable augmentations terminate either with a record preserving every declared response or with proof that no library augmentation removes the loss. For an analytic control germ, integral closures characterize preservation along every analytic control arc, and finitely many Rees valuations detect failure. This connects the state--measurement--record chain to an executable completion-or-refusal procedure, an attainable-Fisher kernel criterion, and finite-sample decisions. A three-qubit calculation separates measurement loss from record loss. Prospectively fixed IBM Kingston and Marrakesh experiments test decisions in four-qubit fixed-particle-number and GHZ families, including negative controls. In two-epoch IQM Garnet data, median record-level drift is 0.0797 times full-distribution drift, but a significant residual remains in 35 of 36 settings. On these circuits, the rules detect loss and approve records only within stated tolerances; they do not establish universal compression performance or device quantum Fisher information.
items.title: Completing or Refusing Low-Dimensional Records of Structured Quantum Circuits: Measurement Loss, Compression Loss, and Hardware Drift

items.summary: This dataset and replication package accompanies a comparative spatial-network analysis of the structural resilience of international digital connectivity across the 32 NATO member states and Russia. The study integrates active international submarine communication cable (SCC) systems with operational cross-border terrestrial fibre connectivity (LCC) and evaluates how much direct external-partner connectivity remains under progressively more severe disruption scenarios. The principal outcome is Partner Retention, defined as the share of baseline direct external partners that remain connected after a disruption. The analysis includes random SCC failures, geographically correlated disruption, complete SCC outage, terrestrial partner concentration tests, alternative clustering thresholds, and additional robustness checks. Under a complete submarine-cable outage, Russia retains 92.3% of its direct external partners, compared with a median of 33.3% among NATO members with active submarine-cable connectivity. The results indicate that this structural advantage is primarily associated with Russia’s extensive cross-border terrestrial fibre network rather than a larger submarine-cable system. The package includes R scripts, processed replication data, selected raw submarine-cable inputs, result tables, figures, QGIS outputs, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, metadata, and methodological notes. The dataset measures structural connectivity rather than traffic volume, bandwidth, latency, economic loss, repair time, or dynamic rerouting capacity.
items.title: Structural Resilience of International Digital Connectivity under Submarine Cable Disruption: NATO Members and Russia

items.summary: Question-answering often requires reasoning across multiple connected facts rather than retrieving a single isolated relation. Knowledge graphs (KGs) provide a structured way to represent such facts, but training large language models (LLMs) only on isolated KG head-relation-tail triples may limit their ability to learn the surrounding context needed for multi-hop reasoning. In this work, we propose a context-augmented training framework for multi-hop question-answering. Although generally applicable, we validate the framework in the context of disease-specific KGs, extracted using a reliable KG extraction framework called GraphMERT, for Gastroparesis and Diabetes. For each primary KG triple, we attach supporting triples extracted from the same source text chunk to form a context graph (CG). This creates two supervision settings: KG-grounded supervision, which uses only the target KG triple or path, and CG-grounded supervision, which uses the target KG triple or path together with supporting context triples. We train the Qwen3-14B model using supervised fine-tuning (SFT) under both settings, producing KGModel and CGModel variants. To strengthen the lower-hop factual foundation of the models, we introduce an LLM-judged, history-aware adaptive repair pipeline that identifies unresolved one-hop failures, continually fine-tunes on targeted repair examples, and removes or quarantines problematic noisy triples. This repair stage enables the models to reach 100% accuracy on the cleaned retained one-hop validation sets. Finally, we employ reinforcement learning (RL) using lower-hop question-answer items and evaluate generalization on harder 3-hop, 4-hop, and 5-hop tasks. Across both diseases, context-augmented supervision consistently improves multi-hop performance over KG-only supervision. RL initialized from repaired SFT checkpoints yields larger and more stable gains.
items.title: Repair Before Reinforce: Context-Augmented Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Multi-Hop Question Answering

items.summary: Martin Scorsese’s 1991 Cape Fear is often remembered as a violent psychological thriller built around Robert De Niro’s grotesque performance as Max Cady, but the film’s deeper force lies in its study of guilt, moral contamination, family breakdown, adolescent vulnerability, and the collapse of legal authority. A remake of J. Lee Thompson’s 1962 film, itself adapted from John D. MacDonald’s novel The Executioners, Scorsese’s version shifts the moral center of the story. In the original, Max Cady largely functions as an external predator who invades the life of a fundamentally decent lawyer and his family. In the 1991 version, Cady becomes something more disturbing: the return of Sam Bowden’s repressed guilt, the embodiment of a legal and moral failure that cannot remain buried. This essay argues that Scorsese’s Cape Fear is not merely a story about a family stalked by a criminal. It is a film about the psychological collapse of respectability under pressure. Through Max Cady, Sam Bowden, Leigh Bowden, Danielle Bowden, Lori Davis, and the compromised figures of law surrounding them, Scorsese turns a home-invasion thriller into a fevered southern-gothic nightmare about guilt, sexuality, punishment, and the terrifying instability of civilized identity.
items.title: The Return of the Repressed: Family Guilt, Moral Contamination and the Psychological Terror of Scorsese's Cape Fear

items.summary: Prompt-policy editing offers a practical way to improve agents that synthesize executable workflows without updating the underlying model. However, persistent prompt editing has two coupled properties. First, edit locality does not imply effect locality: an edit confined to one policy segment can ripple through downstream execution, altering behavior beyond the edited segment. Second, edit effects are composition-sensitive: edits that work in isolation can interfere after composition, causing one or both to lose their benefit or become harmful. Persistent adaptation must therefore support two distinct decisions: identifying where the policy should change from execution feedback, and determining whether the resulting edit remains safe to persist after composition. To address these challenges, we introduce RIPPLE (Replay-Informed Persistent Policy Localization and Editing), which separates where an edit is made from whether it remains safe after composition. It diagnoses failed trajectories, maps each actionable failure to a predefined policy segment, and restricts the correction to that part of the policy. RIPPLE then evaluates candidates against the same iteration-start policy to compare their isolated gains, before replaying promising edits after previously accepted updates to expose downstream effects and interactions. Only edits that remain safe under composition are retained. We evaluate RIPPLE on Flow-HO, a synthetic held-out benchmark for executable workflow synthesis. RIPPLE improves validation success by up to 23.1% and yields positive gains on two additional frozen language-model backbones, while maintaining edit efficiency and low execution cost. Targeted interaction analysis further demonstrates both properties: a segment-local tool-use edit changes downstream resource resolution and validation, while an edit beneficial in isolation becomes harmful after composition.
items.title: Local Edits, Global Ripples: Replay-Informed Policy Adaptation for Workflow Synthesis

items.summary: The Earth That Heard   The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua's altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel's unfinished offering, Cain's failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. This version adds a new chapter on Cain, the altar, and the city of refuge — linking "from My altar you shall take him" (Exodus 21:14) to the Mishnah's ruling that one sentenced without a High Priest never goes free (Makkot 2:7), and to the discovery that Shechem itself is designated a city of refuge in Joshua 20:7. Additional sections trace Jacob's route from Sukkot to Shechem as a draft of Joshua's entry axis, the letter-midrash of "sotho" (Genesis 49:11) as a covering that was never performed, and the mechanical letter-echo of Shaddai hidden in Laban's Aramaic "Yegar Sahadutha" (Genesis 31:47).12:56 PM   The work explicitly separates three epistemic levels: Text — what the biblical text states; Reading — what emerges when distant passages are compared; and Implication — the larger interpretation suggested by the resulting structure. The pattern is tested quantitatively. The present essay contains 136 key verses. Using the Control Alphabet / Mandatory Root morphology developed in The Road and the Place, 100,000 permutations yield T1 = 11.23 and T2 = 24.12, with zero exceedances (p_MC ≈ 10⁻⁵; Phipson & Smyth, 2010). A Leave-One-Book-Out test shows no single Torah book is necessary for the signal (worst case: Genesis removed → Z = 10.61). A Leave-One-Motif-Out test shows no single root is necessary (worst: rbtz removed → Z = 16.01). A book-stratified null (Z = 19.93) confirms the effect is not an artifact of verse distribution. A top-10 ablation (Z = 3.95, p = 0.0013) shows the signal weakens but survives removal of the dominant motifs. A Foundation 12-Letter Split, stripping all 10 control letters rather than 7, yields Z = 4.17 — confirming the framework is not ad-hoc. Six benchmark anthologies were tested: the Ebal/Shechem axis is anomalous in all three validated methods; Covenant remains a positive control but significantly lower; Joseph, Tabernacle, and "the place that He will choose" are negative in all. An independent replication pilot tested whether the signal depends on the author's specific verse choices. Eight semantic criteria were defined — no roots, no letter analysis, no knowledge of any test results — and two independent language models selected Torah verses blind. Model A (243 verses) yielded T2 = 8.70; Model B (252 verses) yielded T2 = 9.84; the consensus of both (142 verses) yielded T2 = 8.51. All with zero exceedances. Only 22% of the essay's verses were also selected. The signal survives independent selection. A pre-registered protocol for three independent human readers is included (protocol hash: a577cb03...). The result does not statistically prove the theological interpretation; it shows that the textual concentration being interpreted is itself measurable and unusual under multiple independent approaches. A dual adversarial computational audit (LLM-assisted) verified the code, reproduced the numbers, identified and corrected all bugs, and rated the statistical appendix at 7.0
items.title: The Earth That Listened — The Hidden Timeline from Genesis to Joshua

items.summary: Production artificial intelligence systems are increasingly assessed not only by whether they generate accurate predictions, but by whether the operating organization can reconstruct, explain, and defend the exact evidence behind an individual outcome after the surrounding system has changed. This paper develops a quantitative framework for measuring that property, which we term evidence continuity. The framework is grounded primarily and foundationally in the work of Mesbaul Haque Sazu, specifically his Governed Decision-Intelligence (GDI) reference architecture [22] and his Full-Stack Production-Platform Reference Architecture [21]. GDI establishes the decision as the unit of assurance and makes evidence binding, lineage, validation, calibrated confidence, deterministic explanation, human oversight, and outcome closure explicit control obligations. The Full-Stack architecture extends these obligations into runtime operation through capture-at-commit, execution records, trajectory-level observability, before-commit gating, and closed-loop production control. Building directly on and leveraging these two foundations, this paper contributes a measurement layer that sits above them. We model an AI system as a typed, versioned, directed evidence graph and introduce three constructs: the Evidence Continuity Graph (ECG), the Trace Completeness Ratio (TCR), and the Governance Coverage Index (GCI). We formalize per-decision and aggregate estimators, extend the naive independence model to a correlated-failure regime using a Beta-Binomial mixture, and derive path-based reconstructability over admissible evidence paths. A synthetic benchmark of 2,800 investigation traces demonstrates how time-to-trace, incomplete-trace probability, and reconstruction probability respond as evidence coverage varies. The results are illustrative rather than empirical claims about deployed systems. The paper concludes with a reference implementation architecture, threshold-setting guidance calibrated to deployment risk, a security and failure analysis, and a research agenda for validating evidence continuity on real production workloads.

items.summary: Production artificial intelligence systems are increasingly assessed not only by whether they generate accurate predictions, but by whether the operating organization can reconstruct, explain, and defend the exact evidence behind an individual outcome after the surrounding system has changed. This paper develops a quantitative framework for measuring that property, which we term evidence continuity. The framework is grounded primarily and foundationally in the work of Mesbaul Haque Sazu, specifically his Governed Decision-Intelligence (GDI) reference architecture [22] and his Full-Stack Production-Platform Reference Architecture [21]. GDI establishes the decision as the unit of assurance and makes evidence binding, lineage, validation, calibrated confidence, deterministic explanation, human oversight, and outcome closure explicit control obligations. The Full-Stack architecture extends these obligations into runtime operation through capture-at-commit, execution records, trajectory-level observability, before-commit gating, and closed-loop production control. Building directly on and leveraging these two foundations, this paper contributes a measurement layer that sits above them. We model an AI system as a typed, versioned, directed evidence graph and introduce three constructs: the Evidence Continuity Graph (ECG), the Trace Completeness Ratio (TCR), and the Governance Coverage Index (GCI). We formalize per-decision and aggregate estimators, extend the naive independence model to a correlated-failure regime using a Beta-Binomial mixture, and derive path-based reconstructability over admissible evidence paths. A synthetic benchmark of 2,800 investigation traces demonstrates how time-to-trace, incomplete-trace probability, and reconstruction probability respond as evidence coverage varies. The results are illustrative rather than empirical claims about deployed systems. The paper concludes with a reference implementation architecture, threshold-setting guidance calibrated to deployment risk, a security and failure analysis, and a research agenda for validating evidence continuity on real production workloads.

items.summary: We prove that every non-trivial rectifiable tame knot embedding K ⊂ R³ has distortion δ(K) > 6.5321. Consequently, the infimum within every non-trivial tame knot type is at least 6.5321. This improves the 6.32 bound in version 1.0 by 0.2121. The new comparison couples an actual last radial crossing on the initial arc with the same actual complementary split point, retaining both cyclic routes and common angular data. items.summary: Martin Scorsese’s 1991 Cape Fear is often remembered as a violent psychological thriller built around Robert De Niro’s grotesque performance as Max Cady, but the film’s deeper force lies in its study of guilt, moral contamination, family breakdown, adolescent vulnerability, and the collapse of legal authority. A remake of J. Lee Thompson’s 1962 film, itself adapted from John D. MacDonald’s novel The Executioners, Scorsese’s version shifts the moral center of the story. In the original, Max Cady largely functions as an external predator who invades the life of a fundamentally decent lawyer and his family. In the 1991 version, Cady becomes something more disturbing: the return of Sam Bowden’s repressed guilt, the embodiment of a legal and moral failure that cannot remain buried. This essay argues that Scorsese’s Cape Fear is not merely a story about a family stalked by a criminal. It is a film about the psychological collapse of respectability under pressure. Through Max Cady, Sam Bowden, Leigh Bowden, Danielle Bowden, Lori Davis, and the compromised figures of law surrounding them, Scorsese turns a home-invasion thriller into a fevered southern-gothic nightmare about guilt, sexuality, punishment, and the terrifying instability of civilized identity.
items.title: The Return of the Repressed: Family Guilt, Moral Contamination and the Psychological Terror of Scorsese's Cape Fear

items.summary: The paper studies finite-horizon ruin for an insurance company with several lines of business admitting heavy-tailed claims. The claim amount process of the insurance company is modeled as a multivariate increasing Lévy process possibly perturbed with fluctuations. A relevant insolvency event may involve the failure of a single line, of several lines at once, or of groups of lines linked through internal transfers, reinsurance, or a guarantee arrangement. These events have different geometries and need not occur on the same probability scale. Under asymptotic tail independence among claims from different lines, classical regular variation assigns zero limiting probability to a multi-line failure and is therefore unable to identify either the ruin probability or the corresponding solvency capital requirement. Using a multivariate Lévy process to model cumulative claims and regular variation on a nested sequence of subcones of the positive orthant to model dependence across lines, we provide the exact scaling rate of the ruin probability and the limit behavior. Additionally, explicit computations are presented for examples with independent business lines, common arrivals of independent claims, Gaussian copula dependent claims, Marshall-Olkin dependent claims, and bipartite insurance networks. Finally, we use Monte Carlo simulations to support our theoretical findings.
items.title: Multivariate Ruin in Lévy-driven Insurance Risk Models under Heavy Tails

items.summary: Question-answering often requires reasoning across multiple connected facts rather than retrieving a single isolated relation. Knowledge graphs (KGs) provide a structured way to represent such facts, but training large language models (LLMs) only on isolated KG head-relation-tail triples may limit their ability to learn the surrounding context needed for multi-hop reasoning. In this work, we propose a context-augmented training framework for multi-hop question-answering. Although generally applicable, we validate the framework in the context of disease-specific KGs, extracted using a reliable KG extraction framework called GraphMERT, for Gastroparesis and Diabetes. For each primary KG triple, we attach supporting triples extracted from the same source text chunk to form a context graph (CG). This creates two supervision settings: KG-grounded supervision, which uses only the target KG triple or path, and CG-grounded supervision, which uses the target KG triple or path together with supporting context triples. We train the Qwen3-14B model using supervised fine-tuning (SFT) under both settings, producing KGModel and CGModel variants. To strengthen the lower-hop factual foundation of the models, we introduce an LLM-judged, history-aware adaptive repair pipeline that identifies unresolved one-hop failures, continually fine-tunes on targeted repair examples, and removes or quarantines problematic noisy triples. This repair stage enables the models to reach 100% accuracy on the cleaned retained one-hop validation sets. Finally, we employ reinforcement learning (RL) using lower-hop question-answer items and evaluate generalization on harder 3-hop, 4-hop, and 5-hop tasks. Across both diseases, context-augmented supervision consistently improves multi-hop performance over KG-only supervision. RL initialized from repaired SFT checkpoints yields larger and more stable gains.
items.title: Repair Before Reinforce: Context-Augmented Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Multi-Hop Question Answering

items.summary: This work considers multi-agent coordination with arbitrary information networks among the agents using a game-theoretic approach. A system designer aims to assign local utility functions to the agents to guide their actions toward a desired system objective. The performance of the assigned local utilities is measured by the well known pure price of anarchy (pPoA) metric that equals the ratio of the system objective at the worst pure Nash equilibrium of the corresponding game to the optimal system objective. Our aim is to derive the utility functions which optimize the pPoA-based performance guarantees for any given information network and system objective. We develop a linear program that derives the optimal pPoA for any arbitrary information network and arbitrary system objective. Our work is the first to solve optimal utility design for arbitrary networks; our techniques generalize previous approaches which considered only the full-information setting. For supermodular objective functions, we prove that counterintuitively, a fully communication-denied utility design is optimal irrespective of the original information network. For submodular system objectives, an exhaustive numerical analysis suggests that the optimal utility design is robust to communication failures even for this case. When the system objective is weighted maximum coverage, the marginal contribution utility design provably optimizes the pPoA for a wide variety of information networks of interest.

items.summary: Structured quantum circuits are often represented by low-dimensional records such as occupation numbers or constraint feasibility rather than by full outcome distributions. A record loses control-dependent information when it merges outcomes whose probabilities respond differently to circuit parameters. We assess this loss without assuming a parametric hardware-noise model. Quantum Fisher information bounds premeasurement sensitivity; Fisher metrics of measurements and recorded statistics describe device-attainable sensitivity. For finite control changes, a Hellinger residual measures the response removed by a record, while its local quadratic term is the conditional covariance of the full-outcome score. Simultaneous confidence bounds support approval, refusal, or deferral. We prove a finite-library completion theorem: executable augmentations terminate either with a record preserving every declared response or with proof that no library augmentation removes the loss. For an analytic control germ, integral closures characterize preservation along every analytic control arc, and finitely many Rees valuations detect failure. This connects the state--measurement--record chain to an executable completion-or-refusal procedure, an attainable-Fisher kernel criterion, and finite-sample decisions. A three-qubit calculation separates measurement loss from record loss. Prospectively fixed IBM Kingston and Marrakesh experiments test decisions in four-qubit fixed-particle-number and GHZ families, including negative controls. In two-epoch IQM Garnet data, median record-level drift is 0.0797 times full-distribution drift, but a significant residual remains in 35 of 36 settings. On these circuits, the rules detect loss and approve records only within stated tolerances; they do not establish universal compression performance or device quantum Fisher information.
items.title: Completing or Refusing Low-Dimensional Records of Structured Quantum Circuits: Measurement Loss, Compression Loss, and Hardware Drift

items.summary: Languishing has predominantly been conceptualised at the level of the person, yet psychological constraint may also be expressed within particular configurations of thought. This qualitatively led mixed-methods study examined how university students’ person-level flourishing and NARMA languishing profiles related to self-identified cognitions that constrained movement towards personally meaningful flourishing futures. Seventy-five consenting participants at a South African university completed a 10-item NARMA Continuum comprising five PERMA-aligned flourishing indicators and five directly assessed NARMA languishing indicators: Negativity, Apathy, Restricted Relationships, Meaninglessness, and Adversity Preoccupation. Participants subsequently described a future flourishing self and completed a structured Target, Understand, Replace, and Nurture reflection. One consenting response contained insufficient substantive qualitative material, yielding 74 cases for qualitative analysis. Reflexive thematic analysis was combined with structured framework coding of three proposed properties of languishing cognition: Yield, the represented change in viable human possibility associated with a thought; Viability, the extent to which remaining possibility could still support meaningful participation; and Trajectory, the orientation of possibility towards narrowing, stalling, redirection, or widening. Quantitative scores were integrated as person-level case attributes. Target cognitions principally concerned anticipated failure or non-attainment (29.7%), stalled effort or mobilisation (20.3%), adversity or uncertainty (20.3%), and inadequacy or insufficient capability (13.5%). Yield was predominantly depletive (95.9%), yet depletion did not determine subsequent Trajectory. Viability was most commonly compromised but retained (56.8%), rather than extinguished, while Trajectory was mixed or redirecting in 48.6% of cases, narrowing in 21.6%, stalled in 16.2%, and widening in 13.5%. Overall flourishing and NARMA languishing were strongly inversely associated, r = -.762, 95% CI [-.843, -.647], p < .001. Exploratory integration showed that person-level flourishing differed across cognition-level Trajectory groups, H(3) = 12.69, p = .005, ε² = .14, whereas overall NARMA languishing did not, H(3) = 5.61, p = .132. Replacement cognitions most often restored agency through incremental progress, behavioural pathways, realistic self-permission, or action despite adversity. The findings support a cross-level distinction between person-level languishing and cognition-level constraint. They further suggest that the psychological significance of a thought may depend not only on its valence or content, but on what viable possibility it changes, what remains usable, and where possibility is oriented next. Keywords: languishing, NARMA, flourishing, cognition, viable human possibility, future selves, Yield, Viability, Trajectory, TURN
items.title: What Does a Languishing Thought Take, Leave, and Make Possible? A Qualitative Study of Yield, Viability, and Trajectory in University Student Cognition

items.summary: Prompt-policy editing offers a practical way to improve agents that synthesize executable workflows without updating the underlying model. However, persistent prompt editing has two coupled properties. First, edit locality does not imply effect locality: an edit confined to one policy segment can ripple through downstream execution, altering behavior beyond the edited segment. Second, edit effects are composition-sensitive: edits that work in isolation can interfere after composition, causing one or both to lose their benefit or become harmful. Persistent adaptation must therefore support two distinct decisions: identifying where the policy should change from execution feedback, and determining whether the resulting edit remains safe to persist after composition. To address these challenges, we introduce RIPPLE (Replay-Informed Persistent Policy Localization and Editing), which separates where an edit is made from whether it remains safe after composition. It diagnoses failed trajectories, maps each actionable failure to a predefined policy segment, and restricts the correction to that part of the policy. RIPPLE then evaluates candidates against the same iteration-start policy to compare their isolated gains, before replaying promising edits after previously accepted updates to expose downstream effects and interactions. Only edits that remain safe under composition are retained. We evaluate RIPPLE on Flow-HO, a synthetic held-out benchmark for executable workflow synthesis. RIPPLE improves validation success by up to 23.1% and yields positive gains on two additional frozen language-model backbones, while maintaining edit efficiency and low execution cost. Targeted interaction analysis further demonstrates both properties: a segment-local tool-use edit changes downstream resource resolution and validation, while an edit beneficial in isolation becomes harmful after composition.
items.title: Local Edits, Global Ripples: Replay-Informed Policy Adaptation for Workflow Synthesis

items.summary: This dataset and replication package accompanies a comparative spatial-network analysis of the structural resilience of international digital connectivity across the 32 NATO member states and Russia. The study integrates active international submarine communication cable (SCC) systems with operational cross-border terrestrial fibre connectivity (LCC) and evaluates how much direct external-partner connectivity remains under progressively more severe disruption scenarios. The principal outcome is Partner Retention, defined as the share of baseline direct external partners that remain connected after a disruption. The analysis includes random SCC failures, geographically correlated disruption, complete SCC outage, terrestrial partner concentration tests, alternative clustering thresholds, and additional robustness checks. Under a complete submarine-cable outage, Russia retains 92.3% of its direct external partners, compared with a median of 33.3% among NATO members with active submarine-cable connectivity. The results indicate that this structural advantage is primarily associated with Russia’s extensive cross-border terrestrial fibre network rather than a larger submarine-cable system. The package includes R scripts, processed replication data, selected raw submarine-cable inputs, result tables, figures, QGIS outputs, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, metadata, and methodological notes. The dataset measures structural connectivity rather than traffic volume, bandwidth, latency, economic loss, repair time, or dynamic rerouting capacity.
items.title: Structural Resilience of International Digital Connectivity under Submarine Cable Disruption: NATO Members and Russia

items.summary: Abstract When does a transformed presentation remain the same for a declared task, what evidence can establish that judgment, and what can a bounded observer safely do with it? This paper separates representation, evidence, control and implementation, giving each an exact mathematical contract. For declared transformations and required observations, contextual indistinguishability determines the greatest observation-preserving congruence. Its quotient is the coarsest lawful representation preserving every demanded observation under every permitted continuation. A reference–current construction applies this result directly to persistence judgments, including breaking outcomes and required provenance. An evidence channel determines the demanded distinctions extensionally exactly when its kernel refines the contextual congruence; failure supplies an indistinguishable pair requiring different answers. For explicitly presented finite systems, the paper provides quotient constructions, separating witnesses, supplementary-information bounds and exact finite-memory criteria. Under declared transition and observation semantics, robust safety is characterized by a greatest fixed point, with checkable winning and losing certificates. Suitable observer quotients preserve the safety computation. Finite controller enumeration and declared sensor catalogues yield exact bounded-memory synthesis and joint resource frontiers; adaptive acquisition is incorporated as action under explicit contracts. The paper also establishes incremental and transport laws, strategic comparison results, and conservative model-to-system safety transfer under stated coverage hypotheses. Representation minimality, safety maximality and bounded implementation attainment remain distinct. Extensional existence does not imply effective discovery or affordability, and mathematical guarantees do not establish physical correspondence. The results characterize what can be preserved, distinguished and safely controlled within declared regimes while exposing the additional assumptions required for implementation and deployment. This public edition updates the previously deposited v19.1 release. It clarifies editorial framing, historical review status and correction lineage while preserving the mathematical content. Earlier versions remain part of the publication history.
items.title: Identity Persistence under Declared Transformations: Contextual Quotients, Evidence Attainment, and the Limits of Bounded Judgment
